Screen readers can read the terminal

Wortel 2026.46.5 · 2026-11-12

Screen readers can read the terminal. Apps that read text aloud or describe the screen, like VoiceOver, ask macOS what an app is showing. Until now Wortel’s terminal told them nothing. It now answers as a text area: they get the text on screen (also after you scroll back), the text you’ve selected with a drag, and where every word sits, so a read-aloud app can highlight each word as it speaks it. They’re told when the screen changes, a few times a second at most, and none of this costs anything until an app asks.

Send Feedback. Help ▸ Send Feedback… opens an email to hello@wortel.sh with your Wortel version, macOS version and your Mac’s chip already filled in, so you can see everything in it before you send.

Better crash reports, less location. If you share anonymous usage data, Wortel now notes whether its last run ended cleanly or crashed, and after a crash it sends where in Wortel’s own code that happened, as numbers only, with no file paths or names. It also counts which agents you start, from a fixed list, and how often sessions are archived. Usage data no longer includes a location looked up from your internet address.

⌘-click a link while an agent has the mouse

Wortel 2026.46.4 · 2026-11-10

⌘-click a link while an agent has the mouse. Codex, and other agents that fill the whole terminal, take the mouse over so they can do their own scrolling and selection. While they had it, ⌘-click on a URL went to the agent and did nothing, unless the agent had made that URL a link itself. URLs in a command, an approval prompt or your own message were stuck. Now holding ⌘ gives the mouse back to Wortel: ⌘-click opens the link, ⌘ over a URL underlines it, and ⌘-drag selects text you can copy with ⌘C, including in Codex’s approval prompt, where a plain drag selects nothing. A plain click or drag still goes to the agent, as before.

No notification for an answer you already read

Wortel 2026.46.3 · 2026-11-10

No notification for an answer you already read. When an agent finished while you were looking at it, and you scrolled through its answer and then switched to another app, a notification quoting that answer could still arrive a few seconds later. Wortel waits for the screen to settle before it calls a turn finished, and your scrolling kept restarting that wait until you had left. Now Wortel checks whether the session was in front of you after the agent last wrote to its conversation, and if it was, it stays quiet. A turn that finishes after you’ve left still notifies you, and so does an error or a question.

Smaller things. A worktree session with its branch on a second line now has its status dots in line with every other row in the sidebar.
